0.headline: Manika Plastech raises Rs 37.6 crore from 4 anchor investors including Trust MF; IPO to open on September 11
0.heading: Manika Plastech raises Rs 37.6 crore from 4 anchor investors including Trust MF; IPO to open on September 11
0.intro: Manika Plastech IPO | The company is raising Rs 92.5 crore through the issuance of fresh equity shares, while promoter entity VRIDAA Holding Trust will sell 76.74 lakh equity shares worth Rs 33 crore through an offer for sale.
0.body:
Manika Plastech, the Mumbai-headquartered plastic products manufacturing company, has raised Rs 37.6 crore from four anchor investors, including Trust Mutual Fund, on September 10, a day ahead of the IPO opening.

The Rs 125.5-crore IPO is set to open for public subscription on September 11, with a price band of Rs 40-43 per share, and will close on September 16.

The company is raising Rs 92.5 crore through the issuance of fresh equity shares, while promoter entity VRIDAA Holding Trust will sell 76.74 lakh equity shares worth Rs 33 crore through an offer for sale (OFS).

Manika Plastech, in its filing with the stock exchanges on Thursday, said it had allocated 87.55 lakh equity shares to four anchor investors at the upper end of the price band.

Pantomath Group subsidiary Wealth Company Asset Management-owned The Wealth Company Alternates Trust-Bharat Value Fund-Series III emerged as the largest investor in the anchor book, acquiring 41.04 lakh shares for Rs 17.6 crore.

Trust Mutual Fund, through its two schemes, picked up 23.26 lakh shares for Rs 10 crore, while Finavenue Capital Trust, through Finavenue Growth Fund, and Nova Global Opportunities Fund PCC, through Touchstone, each bought shares worth Rs 5 crore in Manika Plastech.

Click Here To Read All IPO News

Manika Plastech is a precision-engineered rigid polymer packaging manufacturer, specialising in products such as battery casings, pails and thin-wall containers. Its products cater to several industries, including automotive, energy storage, telecommunications, paints, lubricants, agrochemicals, construction chemicals, food, and dairy.

The company intends to utilise Rs 54.9 crore of the net proceeds from the fresh issue for capital expenditure towards the purchase of plant and machinery, Rs 15 crore for debt repayment, and the remaining amount for general corporate purposes.

Manika Plastech, which operates seven facilities with an installed capacity of 29,200 MTPA, reported a profit of Rs 13 crore and revenue of Rs 162.4 crore for the quarter ended June 2026.

Profit for the fiscal year ended March 2026 increased to Rs 22.4 crore, up 15.9 percent from Rs 19.3 crore in the previous year, while revenue for the same period grew 7.3 percent to Rs 436 crore from Rs 406.5 crore.

Pantomath Capital Advisors is acting as the merchant banker for the Manika Plastech IPO.

1.headline: Veegaland Developers IPO subscribed 62% on Day 1; retail portion leads demand
1.heading: Veegaland Developers IPO subscribed 62% on Day 1; retail portion leads demand
1.intro: The initial public offering (IPO) of Kerala-based real estate developer Veegaland Developers was subscribed 62 percent on the opening day, with investors bidding for 70.26 lakh shares against 1.13 crore shares on offer as of 5:00 pm on September 10, according to NSE data.
1.body:
The initial public offering (IPO) of Kerala-based real estate developer Veegaland Developers was subscribed 62 percent on the opening day, with investors bidding for 70.26 lakh shares against 1.13 crore shares on offer as of 5:00 pm on September 10, according to NSE data.

Retail investors led the demand, with their reserved portion subscribed 82 percent. The non-institutional investor (NII) category was subscribed 39 percent during the period.

The Rs 210-crore IPO, which comprises entirely a fresh issue, is open for subscription from September 10 to September 15. The company has fixed the price band at Rs 130-140 per share.

Read Also: From bank rejection to Rs 11,000 crore net worth: Meet Veegaland founder Kochouseph Chittilappilly who donated his kidney to a stranger at 60


The IPO had received a boost ahead of its public launch after Veegaland Developers raised Rs 63 crore from anchor investors. Nine institutional investors participated in the anchor book, with EQ India Fund emerging as the largest participant after purchasing 10.71 lakh shares for Rs 15 crore at the upper end of the price band.

Swyom India Alpha Fund and Tiger Strategies Fund acquired 7.14 lakh shares and 5.71 lakh shares for Rs 10 crore and Rs 8 crore, respectively. Taurus Mutual Fund, Innovative Value Fund, Visionary Value Fund, VBCUBE Ventures Trust and CP Capital each picked up 3.57 lakh shares for Rs 5 crore.

In the grey market, Veegaland Developers shares were commanding a premium ahead of the issue. InvestorGain showed a grey market premium (GMP) of Rs 25 per share, implying an indicative listing price of Rs 165 against the IPO's upper price band of Rs 140. This translates into a potential premium of around 18 percent over the issue price.

GMP is an unofficial market indicator and can change before listing. It should not be treated as a guarantee of the eventual listing price.

Check IPO News Here

Veegaland Developers plans to deploy Rs 119.82 crore from the net IPO proceeds towards expenses related to the development of its ongoing projects.

The remaining funds will be utilised for unidentified land acquisitions and general corporate purposes.

The IPO is being managed by Cumulative Capital as the merchant banker. The shares are scheduled to be listed on the NSE and BSE on September 18, subject to the issue timetable.

About Veegaland Developers

The company operates under the Veegaland Homes brand in Kerala and is part of the V-Guard Group. Its portfolio comprises 12 ongoing projects and three upcoming projects, spanning residential and other real estate developments. As of June 2026, Veegaland Developers had completed 10 projects with a total saleable area of 11.05 lakh square feet.

2.headline: Arcil IPO booked 87% on second day of bidding; GMP drops to 11%
2.heading: Arcil IPO booked 87% on second day of bidding; GMP drops to 11%
2.intro: The initial public offering (IPO) of Asset Reconstruction Company India (Arcil), backed by Avenue Capital Group and State Bank of India, was subscribed 87 percent as of 5:00 pm on September 10, as per the NSE data.
2.body:
The initial public offering (IPO) of Asset Reconstruction Company India (Arcil), backed by Avenue Capital Group and State Bank of India, was subscribed 87 percent as of 5:00 pm on September 10, as per the NSE data.

The Rs 733-crore public issue received bids for 3,20,04,770 equity shares against 3,69,12,363 shares available for subscription. Retail investors emerged as the strongest participants, with their portion subscribed 1.24 times, while the non-institutional investor category was subscribed 1.03 times.

In the grey market, Arcil shares were trading at a premium of 10.79 percent on September 10, according to InvestorGain. The grey market premium (GMP) is an unofficial indicator of market sentiment and should not be treated as a guaranteed listing gain or return.

Read Also: Steamhouse India IPO subscribed 90% so far on Day 2; GMP at 25%

The IPO comes with a price band of Rs 132-139 per share and will remain open for subscription until September 11. The issue is entirely an offer-for-sale (OFS), meaning Arcil itself will not receive any funds raised through the IPO.

Ahead of the public issue, the company raised Rs 219.89 crore through its anchor book. It allotted 1.58 crore equity shares to 21 institutional investors.

Several prominent global investors participated in the anchor allocation, including Goldman Sachs, Ashoka WhiteOak ICAV, Societe Generale, BofA Securities Europe and Integrated Core Strategies.

Domestic mutual funds also accounted for a significant portion of the anchor placement. Arcil allotted 81.29 lakh shares to 12 schemes managed by six fund houses — White Oak Capital, Aditya Birla Sun Life AMC, Bandhan Mutual Fund, Tata Mutual Fund, JM Financial Mutual Fund and Groww Mutual Fund.

Since the issue is an OFS, the IPO proceeds, after deducting issue-related expenses, will accrue to the selling shareholders. These include Avenue India Resurgence, State Bank of India, Lathe Investment, owned by Singapore's sovereign wealth fund GIC, and Federal Bank.

Arcil reported revenue of Rs 753 crore for the financial year ended March 2026, marking a 26.3 percent increase from Rs 596.4 crore in the previous year. Profit for the year rose 14.8 percent to Rs 407.8 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 355.3 crore in FY25.

Check IPO News Here

IIFL Capital Services, IDBI Capital Markets &amp; Securities and JM Financial are the merchant bankers handling the IPO.

About Asset Reconstruction Company India (Arcil)

Established in August 2003, Arcil was the first asset reconstruction company incorporated in India. It acquires stressed assets from banks and financial institutions and works on their resolution through measures such as restructuring, enforcement of security rights and settlements. The company aims to maximise recoveries from stressed assets while improving the value of the underlying assets.
